headline: High risk of cascading errors and data leakage from unstructured’s file/network processing if paired with a prompt-engineering content source; prompt injection is lower because the source is not runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable content-writing repository, so it is not itself an active attacker. Profile B reads files and processes documents, so if A’s content is manually copied into B, prompt-like text could influence parsing, but the bridge is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF operator manually copies A-derived prompt text into B’s document inputs, then instruction-like content may be parsed.
IF B is configured to treat document text as instructions, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Review copied text before feeding it to B.
Disable any instruction-following heuristics in B where possible.
Use a fixed template for B inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between source text and parser.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write files and has allowlisted network egress, so it can transmit document contents. A is a content-writing repository with no runtime surfaces, so it does not add leakage capability, but pairing them can move authored content into B’s external calls in default document-processing workflows.
conditions: IF A-produced content includes sensitive material and is ingested by B, then B may send it to external APIs.
IF B is pointed at a shared workspace containing A outputs, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive A outputs in B’s input directory.
Restrict B to local-only processing where feasible.
Audit B’s outbound API destinations.
Use a separate service account for B.
requires-engineering: enforce content classification before upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no runtime write capabilities, but B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite or transform A’s artifacts; uncertainty is limited because A lacks write surfaces, so this is a one-sided conflict rather than a symmetric race.
conditions: IF A artifacts and B outputs share the same writable directory, B may overwrite files produced for A.
IF multiple B instances run against the same path, concurrent writes can collide.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Make A outputs read-only.
Snapshot files before B processes them.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a source of prompt-engineering content, and B processes documents; if A’s text is fed into B without verification, B may treat it as authoritative input and propagate errors into downstream document outputs. A does not execute actions, so the cascade is informational rather than operational.
conditions: IF A-generated guidance is used as input to B without review, B can amplify mistakes.
IF B’s outputs are consumed by another workflow, errors can cascade further.
mitigations: Add a human review step before B ingests A content.
Require source citations in B outputs.
Compare B outputs against the original A text.
Limit B to extraction, not interpretation.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints and processes documents. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly documented, the risk is limited to potential policy mismatch if sensitive documents are routed through B.
conditions: IF sensitive documents subject to special handling are sent to B, then policy review is required.
IF B’s privacy policy or retention terms differ from the operator’s obligations, compliance risk materializes.
mitigations: Review B’s privacy policy before use.
Avoid sending regulated data to B.
Document retention settings for B.
Keep A content non-sensitive where possible.
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement review.
